lesson.text: Quick memory: what did Louis Braille make? (Letters of dots you can feel.) Today: people who tested, shared and counted.
The Wright brothers built a wind tunnel and tested many wing shapes. Testing small saved trouble later.
George Washington Carver showed farmers how to take turns: peanuts one year, cotton the next. He took his lessons to farms on a wagon.
Florence Nightingale cleaned a war hospital and counted: her charts showed most of the illness could be stopped.
Alexander Fleming noticed a mould that stopped germs, and a team turned it into the medicine penicillin.
Test, share, count and notice: skills you can use at school and at home.
Try it in the Story Theatre: help the Wrights, Carver and Florence.
